title: Iterative projection based Adaptive Step-Size Geodesic Path Generation Method for automated fiber placement
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beihang University (BUAA) - School of Mechanical Engineering and Automation and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Iterative projection based Adaptive Step-Size Geodesic Path Generation Method for automated fiber placement
detail.abstract: High-quality manufacturing of fiber-reinforced composites via Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) critically depends on layup-feasible path planning. Traditional projection-iteration methods on precise Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models, employ a fixed step size, suffering from cumulative projection errors and limited control over the geodesic curvature. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents an adaptive step-size projection-iteration method for generating geodesic paths. The method centers on developing a dynamic step-size control criterion derived from local differential geometry. This criterion continuously adjusts the iteration step length in real-time based on the local surface normal variation and an explicit upper bound for the permissible geodesic curvature. The step size is reduced in high-curvature regions to bound the projection error, and increased in flatter regions to improve computational efficiency, thereby maintaining geometric feasibility while optimizing the trade-off between path accuracy and computational cost. Subsequently, an iteratively adjusted geodesic offset strategy is applied on the high-precision baseline path to generate a complete set of coverage paths, maintaining a constant geodesic distance between adjacent courses to avoid gaps and overlaps. To validate the proposed method, numerical experiments are conducted on representative models, including a bend plate and a complex free-form surface. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves computational efficiency comparable to fixed-step centerline projection methods while significantly enhancing geodesic curvature control. It also maintains comparable performance in offset spacing uniformity, with outliers lying closer to the theoretical value, facilitating the transition from high-fidelity CAD design to high-quality composite manufacturing in AFP.

title: Demand Response-Oriented Optimization and Control Strategy for Cold Thermal Energy Storage Central Air Conditioning Systems
affiliations: South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Demand Response-Oriented Optimization and Control Strategy for Cold Thermal Energy Storage Central Air Conditioning Systems

keywords: cold thermal energy storage central air conditioning

detail.abstract: Cold thermal energy storage central air conditioning systems often fail to track demand response commands accurately, mainly due to pipeline transport delay and nonlinear electricity-to-cooling conversion in refrigeration units. To address this issue, this paper develops a nonlinear demand response control model with variable flow velocity and proposes a two-stage strategy combining steady-state scheduling and real-time control. In the scheduling stage, nonlinear electricity-cooling conversion and flow-velocity characteristics are linearized and discretized, and the mixed-integer nonlinear model is reformulated as a mixed-integer linear program via McCormick envelope relaxation. In the real-time stage, a sliding mode control law is designed for dual-objective tracking of demand response power and energy. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves demand response tracking accuracy, exploits system flexibility under comfort constraints, and enhances operational economy.

title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading
affiliations: University of Colorado Colorado Springs, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Colorado, Colorado Springs

detail.title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading
detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning trading systems published in the academic literature overwhelmingly rely on price-aggregate state representations (OHLCV bars) or limit-order-book depth features, leaving microstructure pattern theories from the practitioner literature, namely Auction Market Theory and Market Profile, without a peer-reviewed computational instantiation. We present ViperQ, a reinforcement learning system whose state representation is built explicitly from Auction Market Theory primitives: Volume Point of Control, Value Area position, Low Volume Node flags, Cumulative Volume Delta divergence, and tape-velocity signatures, assembled into a 20-dimensional Z-normalised vector. Two Proximal Policy Optimisation agents are trained with a prospecttheory-grounded asymmetric reward function that penalises losing holds at a magnitude consistent with Kahneman and Tversky’s loss-aversion coefficient. Evaluated on a held-out twelve-month partition of institutional tick data the agents have never seen, ViperQ achieves +163.6% ROI on TSLA (-27.5% max drawdown, 27,019 trades) and +116.5% ROI on NVDA (-47.8% max drawdown, 12,892 trades) under zero leverage. The results establish Auction Market Theory features as a tractable structured input modality for sequential decision-making on financial time series and motivate further work on microstructure-aware policy learning.

title: LLMs driven Multi-Factor Quantitative Strategy and Market Anomaly DetectionAnalysis: A Case study of China's A-share market
affiliations: Nanning University, Nanning University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nanning University and Nanning University

detail.title: LLMs driven Multi-Factor Quantitative Strategy and Market Anomaly DetectionAnalysis: A Case study of China's A-share market
detail.abstract: This paper presents TianShu Quant, an LLM-driven platform integrating multi-factor quantitative strategy analysis and market anomaly detection for China’s A-share market. The platform constructs a structured factor library validated through IC analysis and quintile-portfolio back-testing, implements three strategy engines (moving-average crossover, momentum, RSI), and deploys Z-Score anomaly detection alongside LSTM price forecasting. Experiments on CSI 300 constituents demonstrate a Sharpe ratio of 1.21 and factor IC absolute values exceeding 0.03. The platform establishes a reproducible, end-to-end pipeline from raw data acquisition to investment-insight generation.

title: Hierarchical Economic Dispatch Strategy for Energy Management inAC Microgrids Assisted by Renewable Energies with HybridBattery-Hydrogen Storage
affiliations: University Hassan II Casablanca, University Hassan II Casablanca, University Hassan II Casablanca and University Hassan II Casablanca

detail.title: Hierarchical Economic Dispatch Strategy for Energy Management inAC Microgrids Assisted by Renewable Energies with HybridBattery-Hydrogen Storage
detail.abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RES), which are characterized bytheir intermittent nature, alongside hybrid energy storage systems (HESS), necessitatesthe development of advanced energy management strategies capable of simultaneously en-suring economic optimization and operational feasibility in real time. In this paper, ahierarchical energy management strategy based on economic dispatch (ED) using a La-grange multiplier is proposed for AC microgrids incorporating hybrid batteryhydrogenstorage systems. The proposed approach is based on a two-layer architecture. The rstlayer performs a distributed economic optimization to determine the optimal power levelsfor the system's units. The second layer ensures physical feasibility by mapping thesereference values onto the operational constraints of the various subsystems, in particularstorage limits and dynamic constraints. The results of the 24-hour simulation demonstratestable convergence of the Lagrange multiplier, eective coordination between the variousenergy sources, and strict maintenance of power balance in both grid-connected and islandmodes. The proposed strategy also signicantly reduces the use of the diesel generator andimproves the utilization of renewable energy.

title: Application of Digital Twins in the Metaverse for Training in Plastic Injection
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Valencia, Universidad de Alicante, Polytechnic University of Valencia and Polytechnic University of Valencia

detail.title: Application of Digital Twins in the Metaverse for Training in Plastic Injection
detail.abstract: Creating digital twins for training is a Metaverse application. In this study, we analyse its application to plastic injection moulding as a powerful educational tool that can virtually replicate the entire manufacturing process from preparing the mould to the finished product. Based on our previous experience in conventional technical and industrial training, we hypothesized that this technology would help to improve practical learning and theoretical understanding without the need for costly physical installations or wasting expensive materials. With this in view we created a 3D replica of a plastic injection moulding machine with which students could interact by adjusting different parameters such as the mould and material temperatures, injection speed, the pressure applied during the injection cycle as well as plastic cooling and solidification time. This interaction means that the students can see the direct effects of these parameters on the final product without actually using a real machine. The result is a deep learning experience in which they can experiment and see the results in real time, especially helping them to understand the mould-filling stage through the simulated typical parameters of this injection phase. The configurable data presented in the virtual machine had previously been analysed on the Autodesk Moldflow Insight simulation program, while some of the combinations were also tested in the actual process. Two types of materials were analysed in the form of two different parts. Our aim is for the findings of this study to serve as a risk-free training tool for students as well as an industrial resource to cut down on costs and the use of resources. Ultimately, digital twins represent a significant opportunity to transform training in plastic injection moulding as they provide a safe, immersive and optimal learning experience.

title: How Companies Can Discover Strengths from Their Weaknesses
affiliations: Montclair State University, Montclair State University and Montclair State University

detail.title: How Companies Can Discover Strengths from Their Weaknesses
detail.abstract: A widespread pitfall when business managers apply SWOT analysis is regarding all weaknesses as something to be corrected or mitigated. This article proposes a better approach for turning weaknesses into strengths, recognizing that weaknesses and strengths are two sides of the same coin. Using examples of international companies such as 3M, ARM, Red Bull, TikTok, and Pinduoduo, this article provides three concrete approaches for companies to turn their weaknesses into strengths: 1) discover strengths from weaknesses by changing the context; 2) define a game plan to leverage strengths and bypass weaknesses; and 3) create new strengths out of weaknesses via innovation.

title: Modeling Flexible Robust Shortest Path Problem in Citywide Road Networks with Time-dependent Uncertainty
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Jiaotong University, School of Traffic and Transportation, Beijing Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Jiaotong University and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Modeling Flexible Robust Shortest Path Problem in Citywide Road Networks with Time-dependent Uncertainty
detail.abstract: The shortest path (SP) problem plays a crucial role in designing transportation services. However, the dynamic and uncertain nature of the urban road network makes travel plans no longer optimal and reliable, and poses significant challenges to solving the model on large-scale networks This paper proposes a model for finding flexible robust SP in time-dependent uncertainty networks (FRSP-TDU), where dynamics and uncertainty are incorporated into the networks. The concept of flexible factor is proposed to balance the reliability and conservatism of the model. Next, the robust counterpart of the model is derived to eliminate the uncertain nature of the model. In the stage of solution algorithm design, we derive the dual problem of the robust counterpart to reduce the time complexity, and demonstrate that the subproblem of the dual problem is equivalent to the time-dependent (TD) SP problem. Accordingly, we design an exact solution algorithm based on the time-dependent Dijkstra (TD-Dijkstra) algorithm, which can yield optimal solutions in polynomial time. To improve the performance, three speed-up solving strategies are proposed, including merging identical subproblems, shrinking the interest period, and using parallel computing. The effectiveness of the solution algorithm in obtaining exact solutions is verified by comparing it with the brute-force search (BFS) on a case network. In the experimental phase, we first verified the flexible robustness of the model in the Chengdu road network using a real-world speed dataset. the result shows that users can obtain travel plans with different levels of robustness by adjusting the flexibility factor  according to their preferences. After that, calculated performance tests are conducted in several large-scale citywide road networks. Considering the substantial costs associated with real-world data collection, a travel time generation method grounded in the Bureau of Public Roads (BPR) function is developed as the data support for performance tests. The runtime of the FRSP-TDU algorithm can fall within milliseconds and seconds on large-scale networks, comparing with similar researches. This study extends the RSP problem to TDU networks and offers practical value, which can provide more flexible and robust path planning for passengers and resilient travel planning for transportation service design.

title: Risk-prediction-based Robust Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm for Reverse Supply Chain with Demand Uncertainty
affiliations: Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing University of Technology and Beijing University of Technology

detail.title: Risk-prediction-based Robust Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm for Reverse Supply Chain with Demand Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Reverse supply chain (RSC) planning is essential for sustainable resource recovery and circular economy. However, the uncertainty of recycling demand triggers cascading risk amplification across RSC networks, leading to cost escalation and recovery demand losses. To address this issue, a robust multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on risk prediction (RMOEA-RP) is proposed, which can adaptively adjust evolutionary strategies to suppress the risk propagation. Firstly, a cascading risk predictor based on an autoregressive model is built to quantify the sequential propagation of demand uncertainty, enabling the evaluation of node risk backlog. Secondly, a time-aware adaptive evolutionary strategy is designed based on risk scenario similarity to accelerate the evolutionary process via transferring robust solutions under historical risk scenarios to the current scenario. Thirdly, a risk diversion strategy is introduced to refine the planning scheme prior to risk propagation through the reallocation of orders from high-risk nodes to low-load nodes. Finally, the comparative experiments are carried out and operational optimization results demonstrate that the RMOEA-RP can effectively suppress the cascading risk caused by the demand uncertainty, significantly reducing the total costs and demand losses of reverse supply chain planning.

title: Are private equity investors shooting themselves in the foot?
affiliations: Durham University and Durham University

detail.title: Are private equity investors shooting themselves in the foot?
detail.abstract: Private equity investors have a hard time making their decision to commit to a new fund. Their decision process is characterized by a dearth of information; their decisionis not about an asset, but about gauging the capacity of a manager firm to identify, acquire, manage and sell companies. Information desired about the knowledge, networking, institutionalization and ethical practices of the firm can be identified; but accessing adequate data about each of these categories is challenging. Investors resort to creating mosaic of less than accurate information, seeking signals from the market and imposing restrictions on the managers, such as limitations on strategic drift and key person provisions. In so doing, they threat the institutionalization process of private equity firms and favor their mortality. Whether that ultimately benefits investors or not, remains to be seen.

title: Patenting versus Secrecy: Trade Secret Protection and Invention Quality
affiliations: Shandong University at Weihai and The University of Western Australia - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Patenting versus Secrecy: Trade Secret Protection and Invention Quality
detail.abstract: Using China’s 2022 Trade Secret Protection Innovation Pilot in a staggered difference-in-differences design on A-share listed firms from 2019 to 2024, we find that strengthened trade secret protection reduces invention patent filings while leaving utility model and design patents unaffected. R&D intensity rises and firms’ self-reported trade secret reliance increases, indicating substitution toward secrecy on the high-quality innovation margin rather than reduced innovation. Stock illiquidity rises while analyst coverage, media coverage, and Tobin’s Q fall. The patent-type decomposition reconciles apparently conflicting prior findings and informs how transition economies balance innovation incentives against capital-market information efficiency.

title: XFed-IoMT: A Privacy-Preserving Explainable Federated Transformer Framework for Secure Intrusion Detection in Internet of Medical Things Environments  ​
affiliations: Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan

detail.title: XFed-IoMT: A Privacy-Preserving Explainable Federated Transformer Framework for Secure Intrusion Detection in Internet of Medical Things Environments  ​

keywords.keywords: *Federated Learning *Internet of Medical Things *Healthcare Cybersecurity *Intrusion Detection *Explainable Artificial Intelligence *Transformer Networks *Privacy Preservation *Edge Intelligence *Smart Healthcare *Network Securi

detail.abstract: The increasing adoption of intelligent healthcare technologies has accelerated the deployment of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) across modern clinical infrastructures. Smart healthcare devices continuously exchange sensitive medical information through interconnected communication environments, creating substantial cybersecurity challenges for healthcare institutions. Conventional intrusion detection mechanisms frequently rely on centralized architectures that expose healthcare systems to privacy risks, limited scalability, and insufficient interpretability. This research introduces XFed-IoMT, a lightweight privacy-aware federated Transformer framework designed for intelligent intrusion detection within loMT environments. The proposed architecture combines distributed federated optimization, Transformer-based sequential traffic learning, adaptive feature engineering, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to establish a scalable and interpretable cybersecurity framework for healthcare infrastructures. Unlike centralized detection systems, the proposed federated mechanism enables collaborative training among healthcare nodes without direct exchange of raw medical traffic data. The lightweight Transformer module captures contextual communication patterns and temporal network anomalies while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for healthcare edge deployment. To improve transparency and operational trustworthiness, the framework additionally integrates SHAP-based explainability and attention-driven interpretability mechanisms for intrusion reasoning. Experimental evaluation was conducted using CIC-IoMT2024, CIC-IDS2017, and Edge- lloTset benchmark datasets. The proposed framework achieved strong detection performance with high classification accuracy, robust minority attack sensitivity, and reduced false alarm rates across heterogeneous healthcare network scenarios. Comparative analysis demonstrated that XFed-IoMT provides superior privacy preservation, interpretability, and deployment efficiency compared with several conventional machine learning, deep learning, and federated intrusion detection frameworks. title: Trading Up the Chain: Tariff Shocks, Supply Chain Spillovers, and Skill Upgrading in Corporate Hiring
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Trading Up the Chain: Tariff Shocks, Supply Chain Spillovers, and Skill Upgrading in Corporate Hiring
detail.abstract: As global trade frictions escalate and supply chains become more specialized, understanding how external tariff shocks affect factor allocation across firms through inter‑firm linkages is crucial for evaluating trade policy consequences. Using customer-supplier matching data of Chinese listed firms, customs transaction records, and big data from online recruitment platforms from 2016 to 2024, this paper examines how tariff shocks imposed on downstream customers affect upstream suppliers’ labor demand. We find that tariff shocks on customers significantly increase the share of R&D hires among suppliers, shifting labor demand towards higher‑skill positions. Three mechanisms drive this effect: labor cost compression, labor risk avoidance, and the reallocation of R&D labor. The effect is stronger for suppliers that are more dependent on key customers, maintain more stable supply chain relationships, serve more productive customers, or supply customers in high‑tech or capital‑intensive industries. Additional results reveal an asymmetric transmission of trade shocks along the supply chain: tariff shocks on suppliers induce customers to increase demand for operational positions to mitigate short-term supply chain risks, thereby reducing high‑skill recruitment. From a supply chain perspective, this paper provides new micro‑level evidence on corporate labor adjustments to trade shocks, with practical implications for China‑U.S. relations.

title: From Innovation Output to Economic Impact: Measuring the Return on University Research Commercialization in Arizona
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of South Florida and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Innovation Output to Economic Impact: Measuring the Return on University Research Commercialization in Arizona
detail.abstract: Universities are increasingly expected not only to generate knowledge, but also to convert research investment into measurable economic and societal value. Yet conventional assessments of academic innovation often rely on isolated indicators such as patent counts, startup totals, or licensing revenue, which may fail to capture the broader efficiency with which institutions translate research activity into downstream impact. In this study, we introduce the Estimated Economic Impact Efficiency Index (EIEI), a new composite framework designed to estimate the return on university research commercialization by integrating licensing income, royalty streams, startup formation, active licenses, and patent-related option value, normalized to research expenditures. Using recent AUTM and publicly available research expenditure data, we apply the framework to Arizona’s three public research universities: Arizona State University, the University of Arizona, and Northern Arizona University. The analysis reveals sharply differentiated but complementary innovation models. The University of Arizona demonstrates strong impact intensity driven by high-value licensing and royalty performance. Arizona State University exhibits broad commercialization strength through invention volume, startup activity, and entrepreneurial throughput. Northern Arizona University generates meaningful mission-aligned impact relative to institutional scale through regionally focused innovation. Together, these results show that research scale alone does not determine economic return; institutional strategy, sector specialization, and commercialization infrastructure are equally decisive. The EIEI framework offers a practical new tool for benchmarking universities, informing public policy, and evaluating how effectively research ecosystems convert discovery into durable economic value.

title: Voting Powers, Tunneling, and Strategic Trading: Evidence from Chinese Related-Party Transactions
affiliations: Kyoto University

detail.title: Voting Powers, Tunneling, and Strategic Trading: Evidence from Chinese Related-Party Transactions
detail.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between shareholders’ voting powers and tunneling activities. We find that the extent of controlling shareholders’ tunneling activities (measured by related-party transactions and other receivables) is determined by shareholders’ relative influences on voting results in shareholders' meetings. When the largest shareholder can wield significant influences on voting results with a relatively small number of shares, he will conduct more tunneling activities, and vice versa. We also predict that the top shareholders strategically trade their shares. When the largest shareholder can eliminate the threat posed by other shareholders in voting by acquiring a relatively small number of shares, they are more likely to acquire additional shares; conversely, when the largest shareholder can maintain his voting power with a smaller stake, he is more likely to sell shares. We explain the relationship between voting powers and tunneling activities with a rigorous theoretical framework and test its validity using Chinese market data. The empirical evidence strongly supports our theoretical predictions.

title: A systematic approach to state-of-charge estimation using Bayesian filters with linear parameter-varying models for lithium-ion batteries
affiliations: Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE) - Department of Electrical Engineering, Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE) and Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE)

detail.title: A systematic approach to state-of-charge estimation using Bayesian filters with linear parameter-varying models for lithium-ion batteries
detail.abstract: This paper presents a systematic approach to state-of-charge (SOC) estimation using Bayesian filters with linear parameter-varying (LPV) models that account for the dependence of battery behaviour on SOC, current magnitude, current direction and temperature. The proposed approach carefully accounts for the various uncertainties involved in formulating the SOC estimation problem using the state-space representation of the employed model structure. Specifically, two Bayesian filters, namely the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and particle filter (PF), are designed with clear guidelines for selecting the corresponding filter parameters, as opposed to relying on ad hoc tuning. It will be shown that both the EKF and PF provide adequate SOC estimation for NMC and LFP cells, particularly in the absence of a large bias in the current measurements. Moreover, the PF maintains its performance even in the presence of significant bias, owing to its flexibility in specifying arbitrary noise distributions. Finally, the LPV models are compared with LTI models to highlight the importance of identifying high-quality battery models for reliable SOC estimation.

title: Federated Quantum Denoising Transformer with Reconstruction Regularisation for Lithium-Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction
affiliations: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology and University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

detail.title: Federated Quantum Denoising Transformer with Reconstruction Regularisation for Lithium-Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is critical for operational safety and maintenance scheduling in modern energy systems. Data-localisation regulations preclude centralised aggregation of raw cycling records, while pronounced capacity-fade nonlinearity and cell-to-cell variability further complicate collaborative modelling. Although federated learning addresses the data-localisation constraint, existing federated prognostic methods rely on sample-count-weighted aggregation, which fails to capture complex electrochemical ageing dynamics and to stabilise training under heterogeneous client conditions. This paper presents Fed-QDTR, a hybrid federated framework that couples a GRU-based denoising encoder, a multi-head self-attention Transformer, and a four-qubit parameterised quantum circuit (PQC). The PQC performs nonlinear feature transformation with only 24 trainable parameters. A reconstruction decoder enforces latent-space consistency during local training, and a dual-metric aggregation protocol weights client contributions by prediction error and reconstruction fidelity rather than sample count alone, thereby mitigating client drift under non-uniform degradation profiles. Experiments on the NASA and CALCE benchmarks yield mean absolute errors of 0.041 and 0.023, respectively, with convergence within 20 communication rounds. Ablation studies confirm the independent and complementary contribution of each architectural component to the overall predictive performance.

title: Architectures of Stability: A Multidimensional Analysis of Global Safe Havens for Investment and Sustainable Wellbeing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Architectures of Stability: A Multidimensional Analysis of Global Safe Havens for Investment and Sustainable Wellbeing
detail.abstract: Stability, respect for human rights, democracy, and transparency are key points that investment evaluation companies take into account when assigning ratings. This research focuses on analyzing what leading countries in ease of doing business, per capita income, human rights protection, and credit ratings, have done in three areas: the legal, cultural, and ethical components, by 2025. The aim is to identify the actions that have enabled and contributed to these leading countries positioning themselves as safe and attractive destinations for investors, while guaranteeing the quality of life for their populations. This research concludes by highlighting the common actions these countries have taken to become the most attractive to investors and, in turn, leaders in quality of life and human development. It also serves as a guide for countries interested in increasing their economic productivity without jeopardizing human rights.

title: Multiplex Interdependence Centrality: Quantifying Cross-Layer Contagion Risk in Financial Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Multiplex Interdependence Centrality: Quantifying Cross-Layer Contagion Risk in Financial Networks
detail.abstract: Financial institutions today are embedded in a multiplex network of interconnected obligations spanning interbank lending, sovereign bond exposures, and decentralized finance liquidity pools. Traditional systemic risk metrics treat each channel independently, ignoring the cross-layer feedback mechanisms through which shocks amplify during crises. We introduce the Multiplex Interdependence Centrality framework, a spectral measure that computes the principal eigenvector of a weighted supra-adjacency matrix coupling multiple financial layers. The multiplex interdependence centrality score captures a node's systemic importance jointly across all layers, accounting for both intra-layer exposure weights and inter-layer coupling intensities. We couple this centrality measure with a threshold-based cascade simulation to validate its predictive power. Using a synthetic three-layer financial network of 100 nodes representing interbank lending, sovereign bonds, and DeFi markets, we demonstrate that MIC achieves a Pearson correlation of r = 0.806 with actual cascade damage that substantially outperforms the centrality of the eigenvector of the single-layer, PageRank, and the centrality of the differences. Our results provide a rigorous quantitative foundation for integrating multiplex network metrics into institutional risk monitoring, central bank stress-testing frameworks, and regulatory oversight of cross-sector financial contagion.

title: An ensemble spatially enhanced TabPFN framework improves prediction of forest soil organic carbon across China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An ensemble spatially enhanced TabPFN framework improves prediction of forest soil organic carbon across China
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of forest soil organic carbon (SOC) is essential for quantifying terrestrial carbon stocks and understanding climate-carbon cycle feedbacks. However, existing approaches often fail to fully capture spatial dependence and integrate multi-scale predictive information. Here, we developed an ensemble spatially enhanced TabPFN framework (ESE-TabPFN) for predicting SOC across Chinese forest ecosystems. A progressive VIF-Boruta-RFE framework identified 10 optimal predictors from 38 environmental variables representing topography, climate, vegetation, soil properties, and anthropogenic factors. Comparison of seven machine-learning algorithms identified TabPFN as the best-performing baseline model (R2 = 0.58). Incorporating a spatial enhancement strategy integrating multi-scale KNN, IDW-based spatial lag variables, and Gaussian kernel smoothing (SE-TabPFN) increased model performance to R2 = 0.67 while reducing RMSE by 11.4%. The final multi-variant ensemble framework (ESE-TabPFN) achieved an R2 of 0.70, representing a 20.7% improvement over the baseline model. The ESE-TabPFN framework was subsequently applied to generate a 1-km resolution map of forest SOC across China, with a predicted mean value of 5.05 kg C m–2. Predicted SOC exhibited a clear zonal pattern, generally increasing from southern to northern China and with elevation. Comparisons with publicly available datasets revealed strong spatial consistency, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.77. Collectively, our results demonstrated that integrating spatial enhancement with ensemble learning substantially improves SOC prediction and provides a novel framework for digital soil carbon mapping.

title: DPAR-Net: Group-Conditional Art Exam Assessment via Dual-Path Reference Encoding
affiliations: Hubei University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hubei University of Technology, Hubei University of Technology, University of Melbourne - Faculty of Science, Hubei University of Technology and University of Nottingham

detail.title: DPAR-Net: Group-Conditional Art Exam Assessment via Dual-Path Reference Encoding

keywords.keywords: Image aesthetic assessment 、Art exam、Group-conditional ranking 、 Fine-grained assessment

detail.abstract: Image Aesthetic Assessment (IAA) has developed rapidly in recent years, but most existing studies focus on predicting the absolute quality of individual images. In contrast, intra-group relative assessment under a unified evaluation context in art exam scenarios remains insufficiently explored. To fill this gap, we construct the Art Exam Dataset (AED), which contains 3360 art exam works from 93 exam themes, covering three major categories: sketch, quick sketch, and color painting. Based on AED, we propose the Dual-path Reference Encoder with Adaptive Routing Network (DPAR-Net), which provides a preliminary group-conditioned assessment framework for art exam works. DPAR-Net consists of a Dual-path Reference Encoder and an Adaptive Routing Fusion module. The Dual-path Reference Encoder models both a context-aware representation with respect to the group reference and a residual-relative representation that emphasizes sample-wise deviation from the group context. The Adaptive Routing Fusion module dynamically integrates the single-image baseline prediction with two correction candidates according to the sample state. Experiments on AED show that DPAR-Net outperforms representative general aesthetic assessment methods, validating the effectiveness of group-context correction and adaptive routing fusion. This work provides a data foundation and methodological reference for fine-grained ranking assessment of art exam works, and also offers a new experimental scenario for group-conditional aesthetic assessment.

title: Before The Storm: Eigenvalue Concentration and Hidden Fragility in the U.S. Banking Sector
affiliations: National Institute of Technology Raipur and National Institute of Technology Raipur

detail.title: Before The Storm: Eigenvalue Concentration and Hidden Fragility in the U.S. Banking Sector
detail.abstract: This paper discusses the structural fragility in the U.S. banking industry during the 2023 Silicon Valley Bank collapse, the most significant banking system failure since the Global Financial Crisis. Random Matrix Theory and Shannon entropy are used in this study, and two measures: the Concentration Ratio (CR) and the normalised Shannon Entropy (H_"norm" ) are applied to 18 U.S. banking stocks between February 2022 and March 2024. The data-driven and event-based criteria are used to divide the study period into three sub-periods, namely, pre-crisis, crisis, and post-crisis. The findings indicate that the industry was very concentrated before the crisis, with CR = 8.56 and H_"norm" = 0.30 in the pre-crisis period, and only one eigenvalue, which explained 83% of the total variance. The rolling H_"norm" bottomed out 148 days prior to the SVB collapse, indicating that structural weakness existed well before the crisis became a reality. The crisis disrupted this concentration, and post-crisis, the concentration levels stabilised at reduced levels. Bootstrap testing verifies that the pre-crisis period is statistically different from both successive sub-periods (p < 0.001) and suggests the presence of a structural break. The results are consistent with prior findings of diminished post-crisis cross-market interdependence, further strengthening the identified structural change. This study is the first to examine the intra-sector eigenvalue concentration of U.S. banking stocks during the 2023 crisis. The findings suggest that intra-sector eigenvalue concentration may complement existing risk-monitoring frameworks and motivate the development of early-warning systems for structural fragility in financial systems.

title: Optimal Allocation of Flood Water Under Uncertainty forDomestic and Agricultural Use in Arid Areas with Limited Data
affiliations: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

detail.title: Optimal Allocation of Flood Water Under Uncertainty forDomestic and Agricultural Use in Arid Areas with Limited Data
detail.abstract: This study proposes a robust optimization (RO)-based framework for optimal water-resource allocation in the hyper-arid Arava Valley of Israel. Robust optimization is particularly suitable for problems with limited probabilistic information because uncertain parameters are represented through deterministic uncertainty sets rather than exact probability distributions. The proposed framework integrates three main components: (i) forecasting domestic water demand using a multiple linear regression model; (ii) constructing uncertainty sets to capture variability in water availability and consumption scenarios; and (iii) developing a robust allocation model that maximizes water-use efficiency while ensuring reliable performance under adverse conditions. Optimal allocation of the limited resources is therefore an essential problem that allows to narrow the gap between constrained supply and demand due to climate changes.,The model is applied to selected settlements in the Arava Valley, where water scarcity strongly constrains agricultural development and domestic supply. In particular, the proposed model enables approximately 28% more land to be cultivated while maintaining reliable domestic water supply.,The objective function determines the optimal combination of water uses under constraints reflecting regional water availability, land allocation for crops, and alternative within-season irrigation scenarios. Results demonstrate that RO enhances system resilience and improves allocation performance under uncertainty. Compared with current allocation practices, the robust model enables to show that additional land can be cultivated, indicating more efficient utilization of scarce water resources while maintaining reliable domestic supply. The findings highlight the potential of robust optimization as an effective decision-support tool for sustainable water-resource management in arid and uncertainty-prone regions.

title: SNIC: A spectral normalization resistant to illumination conditions for robust estimates of GAI from UAV multispectral measurements
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Forestry University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Northwest A&F University, Northwest A&F University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: SNIC: A spectral normalization resistant to illumination conditions for robust estimates of GAI from UAV multispectral measurements
detail.abstract: Green Area Index (GAI) is a key biophysical trait that underpins crop management decisions and plant breeding programs. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing has emerged as a powerful tool for high-throughput crop phenotyping and precision agriculture, with numerous GAI retrieval methods developed from multispectral imagery. These approaches typically rely on radiance or reflectance calibrated using either a reference panel (PanelCal) or a Downwelling Light Sensor (DLS). However, variable illumination conditions during UAV acquisitions introduce systematic radiometric distortions that degrade retrieval accuracy. To address this limitation, we propose the Spectral Normalization for Illumination-Invariant Calibration (SNIC) method to mitigate illumination-induced artifacts in UAV multispectral imagery. A physically based simulation framework was applied for evaluating radiometric calibration strategies under variable lighting conditions, by coupling the Digital Plant Phenotyping Platform (D3P) with a 3D radiative transfer model, LESS, enabling the generation of wheat canopy reflectance spectra and corresponding GAI values under a wide range of illumination conditions and canopy configurations. Based on the simulated dataset, we also demonstrate that inter-band spectral ratios remain stable under varying illumination conditions, thereby validating the fundamental assumption underlying the SNIC method.GAI retrieval was performed using an XGBoost regression model, and four input strategies (Radiance, PanelCal, DLS, and SNIC) were systematically evaluated on a 6,400-sample in situ dataset. The dataset was split into 3,200 samples under stable illumination conditions and 3,200 samples under variable illumination conditions. Under stable illumination conditions, all methods showed comparable performance, with R2 values of 0.83–0.85 and RMSE values of 0.81–0.83, while DLS performed worse (R2 = 0.71, RMSE = 1.01). Under variable illumination conditions, SNIC consistently outperformed all others, achieving R2= 0.90 and RMSE = 0.63. These results demonstrate that SNIC ensures the robustness of UAV-based GAI retrieval under varying illumination conditions. The proposed method provides a simple yet physically interpretable calibration strategy for enhancing the reliability of UAV phenotyping and precision agriculture applications in real-world operational environments.

title: Geospatial Foundation Models for Mapping Daily Reference Evapotranspiration in Africa
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Geospatial Foundation Models for Mapping Daily Reference Evapotranspiration in Africa
detail.abstract: Timely and accurate estimations of reference evapotranspiration (ETo) are critical for effective water resource management and resilient agriculture planning in data-limited, climate-heterogeneous regions such as Africa. Here, we propose a physics-guided two-stage surrogate modeling framework to enable real-time estimation of daily ETo over Africa using satellite-derived surface solar radiation (Rs) and the TabPFN foundation model. First, a hybrid CNN-Windowed-Attention U-Net architecture was developed and trained using the spectral angle mapper loss to harmonize data from the MODIS Terra and Aqua sensors, thereby improving spatial coverage across Africa. Next, to capture radiative transfer processes, we build a surrogate model emulating MCD18A1.062 Rs from top-of-the-atmosphere reflectance and conditioning variables. Then, ETo was estimated in two ways: a physics-guided approach using surrogate Rs and a direct, end-to-end, data-driven approach. The framework was also evaluated against the widely adopted empirical methods, namely Priestley–Taylor, Makkink, Hargreaves–Samani, and Abtew, calibrated, in turn, against the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith as a reference. For Rs, results demonstrate that the surrogate model accurately reproduces Rs variability, with an RMSE of 2.03 MJ.m⁻².day⁻¹. For ETo, TabPFN improves from an RMSE of 0.93 mm.day⁻¹ in the end-to-end approach to 0.79 mm.day⁻¹ in the two-stage approach, outperforming both classical machine learning models and empirical formulations. Furthermore, continental and regional evaluations across nine IPCC climate regions show improved generalization of TabPFN across diverse hydroclimatic regimes, with RMSE values ranging from 0.26 to 0.91 mm.day⁻¹. In contrast, although they require difficult-to-obtain variables, empirical models exhibit systematic errors and limited adaptability to regional variability, with RMSE ranging from 0.49 to 2.94 mm.day⁻¹. With no reliance on costly ground measurements and being fully based on remotely sensed data, this framework can support timely estimation of irrigation water needs across Africa.

title: Evaluation of Tourism Carrying Capacity for Beach Management in Vietnam
affiliations: Vietnam National University Hanoi, Vietnam National University Hanoi, Vietnam National University Hanoi, Vietnam National University Hanoi and Nha Trang University

detail.title: Evaluation of Tourism Carrying Capacity for Beach Management in Vietnam
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the impacts of tourism activities on selected representative beaches in Vietnam, focusing on Nhat Le Beach (Quang Binh Province) and Sam Son Beach (Thanh Hoa Province), and proposes sustainable management solutions. Through field investigations, questionnaire surveys, and data collection and analysis, and carrying capacity assessment methods the results reveal that the carrying capacities of Nhat Le Beach are as follows: the Physical Carrying Capacity (PCC) is 115,200 visitors/day, the Real Carrying Capacity (RCC) is 3343,778227 visitors/day, and the Effective Carrying Capacity (ECC) is 3383523,258 visitors/day. In comparison, Sam Son Beach shows higher capacities, with a PCC of 360,000 visitors/day, an RCC of 97,056 visitors/day, and an ECC of 67,517 visitors/day. During peak periods, the visitor number at Sam Son (69,890 visitors/day) nearly reaches its RCC threshold, indicating potential risks of environmental and infrastructure overload. Based on these findings, the study proposes sustainable tourism management strategies for typical coastal areas in Vietnam.

title: Linking Nighttime Satellite Data with Provincial GRDP in Vietnam: Validation of VIIRS VNL V2
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City

detail.title: Linking Nighttime Satellite Data with Provincial GRDP in Vietnam: Validation of VIIRS VNL V2
detail.abstract: Satellite-derived nighttime lights (NTL) have become widely used proxies for economic activity where traditional statistics are sparse or delayed. This paper studies Vietnam’s 60 provinces during 2018 - 2021 using the annual VIIRS Nighttime Lights (VNL V2) product to estimate elasticities between (i) total radiance and gross regional domestic product (GRDP) and (ii) mean radiance and GRDP per capita. We employ panel-data models with province and year fixed effects (within estimator) alongside cross-sectional between estimators. We find robust, positive elasticities: within-province elasticities of GRDP with respect to total light around 0.19 - 0.25 and between-province elasticities around 0.74 - 1.35; for GRDP per capita with respect to mean light, within elasticities range 0.11 - 0.25 and between elasticities 0.22 - 0.39. Heterogeneity analyses indicate stronger predictive power in more densely populated provinces and larger within elasticities for provinces with lower urban land shares. We discuss implications, limitations of NTL proxies, and avenues for integrating NTL into official statistics and real-time economic monitoring in Vietnam.

title: High-Fidelity Impedance Reconstruction under Dynamic Conditions: An Adaptive Calibration Framework Integrating Harmonic Excitation and Shallow Neural Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology - MIIT Key Laboratory of Critical Materials Technology for New Energy Conversion and Storage, Shenzhen University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Shenzhen University

detail.title: High-Fidelity Impedance Reconstruction under Dynamic Conditions: An Adaptive Calibration Framework Integrating Harmonic Excitation and Shallow Neural Networks
detail.abstract: Real-time monitoring of internal states during operation is critical for ensuring battery safety. While electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) has gained traction as a nondestructive diagnostic tool, its application under high-power operating conditions remains restricted. This limitation primarily arises because traditional EIS (TEIS) measurements require the battery to be in thermodynamic equilibrium, necessitating a relaxation period prior to testing. However, batteries operating under heavy currents exhibit strong polarization, which induces distortion in the measured impedance spectra. Additionally, the reliance of TEIS on highly precise sinusoidal excitations further impedes its implementation in practical scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a dynamic impedance acquisition framework that combines harmonic excitation-based impedance extraction with data-driven calibration, enabling the real-time retrieval of impedance profiles during battery operation. Specifically, square-wave current signals are actively injected during the discharge process. Both the excitation current and the corresponding voltage response are then processed via the S-transform to derive the square-wave EIS (SEIS) across the 0.25–1000 Hz frequency range. Machine learning algorithms are subsequently deployed to calibrate the extracted SEIS. The calibrated SEIS exhibits consistency with the TEIS baseline, achieving an overall root mean square error (RMSE) of less than 0.124 mΩ and a Procrustes similarity greater than 0.997. Furthermore, we systematically investigate the impact of square-wave parameters (period, amplitude, and direct current bias) on the SEIS and evaluate the calibration efficacy across different machine learning models. Leveraging the calibrated SEIS, we perform state of health prediction, yielding an RMSE of 0.8%.

title: Impact of Covid-19 on Stock Markets: Evidence from Global Contagion
affiliations: Queen Mary University of London, Queen Mary University of London and University of Illinois Springfield

detail.title: Impact of Covid-19 on Stock Markets: Evidence from Global Contagion
detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent government policy responses on international stock market contagion. Local infection and mortality rates increase the likelihood of contagion, with mortality rates demonstrating a greater impact. Economic support policies mitigate stock market contagion, yet their effects vary across countries in both timing and intensity. For developing nations, global infections and deaths have a more substantial effect on the likelihood of contagion, whereas for advanced nations, local cases exert a stronger influence. Our results guide governments and international policymakers to contain contagion and alleviate the impact of exogenous shocks worldwide.
